question.text: The line <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>≡</mo><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> touches the circles <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>. Centers of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are <math><msub><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>(</mo><mn>1,2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> respectively Then, the length (in units) of the transverse common tangent of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Note that A1 and A2 lie on different sides of L1,

hence L1 is a transverse common tangent
Radius of C1=3-8+15=45
Radius of C2=9-4+15=65
A1A2=4+1=5
⇒ Length of the transverse common tangent is A1A22-r1+r22=5-22=1 unit
